question: is the ASR effect about WHICH direction, or HOW MUCH cell-mean spread it removes?

verdict.reading: d_naive carries 94% of d_surface's dose and produces a 38% LARGER effect (+0.0586 vs +0.0424, 29 vs 21 flips). READ THIS NARROWLY: cos(d_surface, d_naive) = 0.9613, so this is NOT 'a different direction wins' -- it is a ~16-degree rotation of the same direction doing somewhat more. The near-collinearity is not a coincidence: see dose_identity_bound, which shows a direction at this dose is FORCED to have |cos| >= ~0.95 with d_surface. What it does establish is that the 2x2's identification step (which is the whole difference between d_naive and d_surface) buys no behavioural effect and in fact costs some. d_context, at 0.13 dose -- inside the in-subspace controls' own dose range -- moves ASR by +0.0000, which the dose account predicts and which therefore carries no information about meaning.

caveat: delta_over_dose is only comparable between directions of SIMILAR dose; the dose-response saturates, so comparing it across a 6x gap is the error this script exists to expose.
